nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِها وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحاوُرَكُما إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ (1) قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِها: Abū Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad said: if you wish, you assimilate (idghām) the dāl into the sīn and say: قد سمع, because the place of articulation of the dāl and the sīn is both from the tip of the tongue; and if you wish, you pronounce it distinctly and say: قد سمع الله, because the dāl and the sīn, even though they are both from the tip of the tongue, are not from one and the same place, since the dāl, the tāʾ and the ṭāʾ are from one place, and the sīn, the ṣād and the zāy are from one place — they are called the whistling letters (ḥurūf al-ṣafīr); and moreover the sīn is separate from the dāl [Translator's note: i.e. in a separate word]. [Translator's note: the printed text spells both forms identically; the first is meant with assimilation (qas-samiʿa), the second with clear dāl.]
وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ i.e. the woman who disputes complains to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, of what [befell her] through her husband's ẓihār and asks Him for relief. وَاللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحاوُرَكُما i.e. the conversation of the Prophet ﷺ and the woman who disputes. إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ i.e. of what they both say and other than it. بَصِيرٌ of what they both do and other than it.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: الَّذِينَ is nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject); and according to the view of Sībawayh it may be in the position of an accusative by بصير. يظّهارون is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ; Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read يظهرون [Translator's note: i.e. yaẓẓāharūn, as the vowelling is not shown]; and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and ʿĀṣim read يَظْهَرُونَ [Translator's note: so printed; ʿĀṣim's reading is known as yuẓāhirūn]. Al-Kisāʾī related that in the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy there is يتظاهرون, which is an argument for whoever reads يظهرون [Translator's note: i.e. yaẓẓāharūn], because the tāʾ is assimilated into the ẓāʾ. More sound than this is what Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated from his father from Hārūn, who said: in the codex of Ubayy there is يتظهّرون, which is an argument for whoever reads يظّهرون, because the tāʾ is likewise assimilated into the ẓāʾ. مّا هنّ أمّهاتهم: [أمّهاتهم is] the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which is likened to ليس. Al-Farrāʾ said: [the underlying form is] بأمهاتهم; when the bāʾ was omitted, a trace of it remained, so it put the noun in the accusative. إِنْ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّائِي وَلَدْنَهُمْ: mubtadaʾ and khabar, and «إن» has the meaning of «ما». وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنْكَراً مِنَ الْقَوْلِ i.e. what is not sound. وَزُوراً: Qatāda said: i.e. a lie. منكرا and زورا are accusative by يقولون; if you made it nominative, the meaning would be reversed. وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ i.e. possessor of pardon and forbearance toward whoever repents. غَفُورٌ to him, not punishing him after repentance. And it is said [that] this [was revealed] because in the Jāhiliyya they used to divorce by ẓihār. Abū Qilāba said: in the Jāhiliyya, when a man pronounced ẓihār upon his wife, it was an irrevocable divorce and he could never return to her; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down this.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: the scholars disagree about the meaning of the "return" (al-ʿawd). Some of those who hold to the literal sense (al-ẓāhir) said: expiation is not obligatory upon him until he pronounces ẓihār a second time, and they related that from Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ashajj. Qatāda said: ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِما قالُوا is that after the ẓihār he resolves to have intercourse with her and to approach her. Some of the jurists said: his return is that he keeps her and does not divorce her after the ẓihār, so the expiation becomes obligatory upon him. Al-Qutabī said: it is that he returns to what used to be said in the Jāhiliyya. Abū l-ʿĀliya said: لِما قالُوا i.e. concerning what they said. Al-Farrāʾ said: لما قالوا, إلى ما قالوا and فيما قالوا are one and the same; he means: they go back on their statement. Al-Akhfash said: there is a fronting and a postponement in it, i.e. "then the freeing of a slave for what they said". Among the clearest of them is the view of Qatāda, i.e. then they return to the prohibition which they had uttered and make it lawful. فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ, or "then upon them is the freeing of a slave"; and according to the Basran grammarians فتحرير رقبة is permissible [Translator's note: presumably in the accusative, فَتَحْرِيرَ رَقَبَةٍ, i.e. "then let them free…"; the printed text does not show the vowelling]. مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا: before the man touches the woman, and before the woman touches the man. This is general, except that Sufyān used to say: [it is permitted] to him what is short of intercourse.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
مِنْ [Translator's note: i.e. مَن] is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "so whoever does not find the slave" — and the object is omitted when the meaning is known — "then upon him is the fasting of two months". صيام شهرين [Translator's note: presumably with tanwīn, ṣiyāmun shahrayni] is permissible on the basis that شهرين is an adverb (ẓarf); and if you wish it is an object by way of extension (ʿalā l-saʿa). But when you say صيام شهرين [Translator's note: i.e. in construct], it cannot be an adverb. On this basis Sībawayh related, among [verbs] that pass over to two objects: [Rajaz] 470-
يا سارق اللّيلة أهل الدار
(O you who rob the people of the house tonight)
 فَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَإِطْعامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً i.e. whoever is unable to fast because of old age or chronic illness, then upon him is the feeding of sixty poor people; and tanwīn on إطعام is permissible. "Before they touch one another" is not [stated] here, but it is taken from consensus. ذلك ليؤمنوا بالله ورسوله [Translator's note: so in the source; the muṣḥaf has ذلِكَ لِتُؤْمِنُوا]: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. that severity; and someone else said: We did that so that you would believe in Allah and His Messenger, i.e. so that you would affirm what has come to you and so believe. وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ i.e. these are the obligations of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, which He has delimited. وَلِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ i.e. for whoever disbelieves in them.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ i.e. they oppose Allah and His Messenger and place themselves in the boundary (ḥadd) of His enemies.
كُبِتُوا i.e. they were enraged; and some of the lexicographers said: i.e. they perished. He said: and the original is كبدوا, from their saying كبده when he struck him with a pain in his liver (kabid). كَما كُبِتَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ: the kāf is in the position of an accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar (verbal noun). ولهم عذاب مهين [Translator's note: so in the source; the muṣḥaf has وَلِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ].

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ: what governs يوم is «عذاب». According to the Basrans it may not be indeclinable (mabnī) when an imperfect verb comes after it; it is only made indeclinable when a past verb or something not declinable comes after it — when it is like that, it is made indeclinable, because since it needs what comes after it and cannot do without it, it is treated like it. As for the Kufans, they say: it is made indeclinable only because it has the meaning of إذا, so it is made indeclinable because of its [i.e. إذا's] indeclinability. جَمِيعاً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. on the day when Allah raises them from their graves to the Resurrection in the state of being gathered together. فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما عَمِلُوا i.e. He informs them of what they kept secret and concealed and other than those two among their deeds. أَحْصاهُ اللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ i.e. He counted it, recorded it and preserved it, while those who did it forgot it. وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ i.e. over everything of their deeds a witness, knowing it.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: I.e. have you not seen with the eye of your heart, so that you know that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, nothing small or great being hidden from Him — so how could the deeds of these people be hidden from Him? ما يَكُونُ مِنْ نَجْوى ثَلاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رابِعُهُمْ: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: He, the Exalted, is above His Throne, and His knowledge is with them. ثلاثة is genitive as a badal (substitute) for «نجوى»; it may be genitive by the annexation of نجوى to it; it may be nominative according to the position of نجوى; and it may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun that is in نجوى. إِلَّا هُوَ رابِعُهُمْ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. Al-Farrāʾ related that in the codex (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] there is ولا أربعة إلّا هو خامسهم, and Abū Ḥātim related that in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh there is: ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلّا الله رابعهم ولا خمسة إلّا الله سادسهم ولا أقلّ من ذلك ولا أكثر إلّا الله معهم إذا انتجوا. Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading, if it is authentic, is only by way of explanation (tafsīr); it may not be recited except on that basis. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read ما تكون من نجوى ثلاثة; this reading, even though it differs from the authority of the majority, agrees with the written text (al-sawād) and is permissible in Arabic, because نجوى is feminine in form and «من» in it is redundant (zāʾida), just as you say: ما جاءني من رجل and ما جاءتني من امرأة. The implied form is: "and there is no secret conversation of four but He is the fifth of them". Hārūn related from ʿAmr from al-Ḥasan that he read وَلا أَدْنى مِنْ ذلِكَ وَلا أَكْثَرَ [Translator's note: i.e. وَلا أَكْثَرُ in the nominative, as the following remark implies; the print does not show it] إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمْ, conjoining it to the position. ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما عَمِلُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ i.e. then He will inform them of what they conversed secretly about. إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ of their secret conversations and their confidences and their other deeds and the deeds of His servants.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
Mujāhid said: they are a group of the Jews. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read ينتاجون بالإثم والعدوان [Translator's note: so printed; Ḥamza's reading is known as يَنْتَجُونَ]; and يتناجون is clearer, because they have agreed on reading إذا تناجيتم فلا تتناجوا — except for something narrated from Ibn Masʿūd, that he also read وينتجون بالإثم والعدوان وعصيان الرسول [Translator's note: so in the source; the muṣḥaf has وَمَعْصِيَتِ الرَّسُولِ]. وَإِذا جاؤُكَ حَيَّوْكَ بِما لَمْ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ اللَّهُ: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned its meaning. وَيَقُولُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَوْلا يُعَذِّبُنَا اللَّهُ بِما نَقُولُ i.e. why does He not punish us for that at the time we say it? حَسْبُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ يَصْلَوْنَها فَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. The grammarians related that one says:
حسبك, and no khabar is pronounced for it because its meaning is known; and it is said: it carries the meaning of a command, because its meaning is "refrain"; so since a command is not given a khabar, the khabar of what has its meaning was omitted.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا تَناجَيْتُمْ فَلا تَتَناجَوْا بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ وَمَعْصِيَةِ الرَّسُولِ: there are three ways in it: فلا تتناجوا with two tāʾs; ولا تناجوا with a single tāʾ; and ولا تناجوا with the tāʾ assimilated into the tāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. فَلَا تَنَّاجَوْا; the print does not show the doubling]. Whoever brings it with two tāʾs says: it is a word begun with, separate from what is before it. Whoever brings it with one tāʾ omitted [one] because of the meeting of the two tāʾs, like تذكرون and تتذكّرون. Whoever assimilates says: two identical letters have met with an alif before them, and an assimilated letter may come after an alif, as in دواب. وَتَناجَوْا بِالْبِرِّ i.e. with what brings you near to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. وَالتَّقْوى i.e. with fearing Him by performing His obligations and avoiding what He has forbidden. وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ i.e. to whom is your destination and your gathering, so He will recompense you for your deeds.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
إِنَّمَا النَّجْوى مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ: the soundest of what has been said about it is the view of Qatāda. He said: the hypocrites used to converse secretly in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and that would grieve the Muslims and weigh heavily upon them, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down: إِنَّمَا النَّجْوى مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ لِيَحْزُنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا, the verse. What shows the correctness of this view is the Qurʾān before it and after it. Ibn Zayd said: a man would converse privately with the Prophet ﷺ about a need, and he would do that so that people would see that he had conversed privately with the Prophet ﷺ; then Iblīs would whisper to the Muslims, saying: "This private conversation is only about forces that have gathered against you and some matter that has come up which is intended against you", so they would grieve at that. There is a third view on the verse, mentioned by Muḥammad ibn Jarīr. He said: Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ narrated to us, saying:
Yaḥyā ibn Dāwūd al-Bajalī narrated to us, saying: ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī was asked, while I was listening, about dreams, and he said: dreams are of three ranks. Among them is what Satan whispers, and that is the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: إِنَّمَا النَّجْوى مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ لِيَحْزُنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا; among them is what a man tells himself and then sees in his sleep; and among them is a taking by the hand. And it is read لِيَحْزُنَ [Translator's note: i.e. the alternative vowelling, لِيَحْزُنَ vs. لِيُحْزِنَ, which the print does not distinguish], and the first is more eloquent. وَلَيْسَ بِضارِّهِمْ شَيْئاً إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: i.e. by the decree and determination of Allah; and it is said: بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ — by what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has permitted in it, namely their distress over the believers, because He, exalted be His praise, has permitted that. وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ i.e. let them entrust their affair to Him, and let not the secret conversation and what the hypocrites confide to one another grieve them, since Allah, Majestic and Mighty, protects them and guards them.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: في المجلس: it is narrated from al-Ḥasan and Qatāda that they both read إذا قيل لكم تفاسحوا. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is like تعهدت ضيعتي and تعاهدت. The lexicographers said: تعهّدت is more eloquent because it is an act by one person; and al-Khalīl said: one only says تعهّدت because it is an act by one person. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim read فِي الْمَجالِسِ, and the reading of the generality is في المجلس. Abū Jaʿfar said: the scholars disagreed about its meaning. It is authentically reported from Mujāhid that he said: it is the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ specifically; and it is authentically reported from Qatāda that he said: people used to vie with one another in the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ, hardly any of them making room for another, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down this, meaning that. It is narrated from Qatāda that it concerns the gathering of remembrance (majlis al-dhikr); and al-Ḥasan and Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb said: this is about fighting specifically. Abū Jaʿfar said: the apparent sense of the verse is general, so it must be taken accordingly, and this will then apply to the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ specifically, to war and to gatherings of remembrance — and we know of no fourth view; and the meaning conveys the meaning of "assemblies" (majālis). Moreover, when a person is addressed to make room in his seat and with him is a group who have been commanded with what he was commanded, they have become assemblies. يَفْسَحِ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ is the response to the command, and it carries the meaning of requital (al-mujāzāh). And a فسيح place, i.e. a spacious one. وَإِذا قِيلَ انْشُزُوا فَانْشُزُوا is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ and Shayba; and the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and the people of Kufa is انْشُزُوا فَانْشُزُوا [Translator's note: the two readings are unshuzū (with ḍamma) and inshizū (with kasra); the print does not distinguish them]. They are two dialects with one meaning, and Abū ʿUbayd prefers the second. If a preference could occur in this, the ḍamma would be more fitting, because it is an intransitive verb like قعد يقعد, since most commonly in the speech of the Arabs what is intransitive comes with ḍamma, and what is transitive comes with kasra, like ضرب يضرب. As for the meaning, the soundest of what has been said about it is that it is rising up to every good: commanding right and forbidding wrong, or fighting an enemy, or dispersing from the Prophet ﷺ so that no harm reaches him. يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجاتٍ: it is said: i.e. He raises them in reward and honour; and it is said: He raises them, from elevation, i.e. He raises them above others who do not know, in order to make their excellence clear. وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ i.e. He is informed of it and will requite it.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: they had troubled the Prophet ﷺ with the great number of their private consultations, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, wished to lighten [the burden] on him and commanded them with this; so they held back from private consultation. Then He made it broad for them and did not make it narrow. Mujāhid said: no one acted upon this verse except ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him: he gave a dīnār in charity and then consulted the Prophet ﷺ privately; then it was abrogated. And he [ʿAlī], may the mercy of Allah be upon him, said: through me [the burden] was lightened for this community. The Prophet ﷺ said to me: "What do you think — should whoever consults privately give a dīnār in charity?" I said: "No." He said: "Then a dirham?" I said: "No." He said: "How much, then?" I said: "A grain of barley." He said: "You are indeed one who asks little (zahīd)." Then the lightening was sent down. فَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ i.e. He does not burden one who does not find [the means].

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: The origin of al-ishfāq in the language is caution and fear; and because of this it is not lawful for anyone to describe Allah, Majestic and Mighty, with ishfāq, nor to say: "O Shafīq". Mujāhid said: أأشفقتم i.e. did it weigh hard upon you? فَإِذْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا وَتابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ: so since He has turned to you [in forgiveness], He did not hold them to account. فأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة i.e. then do that whose obligation has not been lifted from you. وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ i.e. in what He has commanded you. وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ i.e. and He will requite you for it.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا قَوْماً غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ i.e. have you not looked with the eye of your heart and seen them? ما هُمْ مِنْكُمْ وَلا مِنْهُمْ: the pronoun refers back to الذين, and they are the hypocrites: they are not of the believers, i.e. of the people of their religion and creed, nor of those with whom Allah is angry, and they are the Jews. وَيَحْلِفُونَ عَلَى الْكَذِبِ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ: they swear that they are believers.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: ما is in the position of a nominative, i.e. evil is the thing which they do, namely their deceiving the believers and their sincere counsel to the disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ جُنَّةً i.e. they took their swearing to the believers that they are of them as a barrier for their blood and their property. And this is the meaning of فَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ, because the way of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, regarding the idolaters is that they be fought, and regarding the People of the Book that they be fought unless they pay the jizya; so when these people displayed faith while being disbelievers, they turned the believers away from fighting them by what they displayed.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: I.e. you will not benefit from wealth so as to ransom yourselves with it [Translator's note: so in the source, in the second person], and their children will not benefit them so as to help them and rescue them from the punishment they are in. أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ: the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) is permissible outside the Qurʾān.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعاً فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ i.e. they will swear to Him upon falsehood; and this is a clear proof of the falsity of the view of whoever said: no one will speak on the Day of Resurrection except the truth, because of what he witnesses.
وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ i.e. on something that benefits them. أَلا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْكاذِبُونَ: إنّ is with kasra because it is at the start [of a sentence]; and I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān permit it with fatḥa, because the meaning of ألا is "truly" (ḥaqqan).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطانُ فَأَنْساهُمْ ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ: this is among what has come in its original form; had it come with the weakening (iʿlāl) [of the weak letter], it would have been استحاذ, just as one says: استصاب فلان رأي فلان, and one does not say استصوب. Abū Jaʿfar said: what comes in its original form is only among what is taken by hearing from the Arabs, not among what is used as a basis for analogy. And it is said: the four-letter [i.e. derived] verb is weakened following the three-letter one; so since one says استحوذ عليه when he overcomes him, and does not say حاذ with this meaning — one only says حاذ الإبل when he gathers the camels — since it has no three-letter [counterpart], it came in its original form.
أُولئِكَ حِزْبُ الشَّيْطانِ أَلا إِنَّ حِزْبَ الشَّيْطانِ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ: his party (ḥizb) is his allies, his followers and his hosts; and the loser (al-khāsir) is the one who has lost in his bargain.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ: Qatāda said: they show enmity to Him; Mujāhid said: they oppose [Him]; and it is said:
its meaning is: they contravene the limits (ḥudūd) of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, in what He has commanded. Its literal sense in Arabic is: they come to be in a boundary (ḥadd) other than His boundary which He has delimited. The original is يحاددون, and the dāl was assimilated into the dāl. أُولئِكَ فِي الْأَذَلِّينَ i.e. among those whom abasement overtakes; and أولئك and what follows is the khabar (predicate) of الذين.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا وَرُسُلِي: it is said: i.e. He wrote in the Preserved Tablet; and al-Farrāʾ made it figurative, making كتب have the meaning of «قال», i.e. Allah [said]: I will surely prevail, I and My messengers, i.e. over whoever opposes Us. «ورسلي» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the implied pronoun that is in «لأغلبن», and «أنا» is a tawkīd (emphasis). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the eloquent usage. All the grammarians permitted in poetry: لأقومنّ وزيد [Translator's note: i.e. conjoining to the nominative pronoun without an emphasizing pronoun]. The Kufans and a group of the theorists permitted conjoining to the nominative implied pronoun without tawkīd, because it occurs both attached and detached, and so differs from the genitive implied pronoun. إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ i.e. possessor of strength and power to [carry out] what He wrote concerning whoever opposes Him and opposes His messengers. عَزِيزٌ in His retribution; no one is able to avenge himself on Him.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
The soundest of what has been narrated about this is that it was revealed concerning the hypocrites who befriended the Jews, because they do not acknowledge Allah, Majestic and Mighty, in the way He must be acknowledged, nor do they believe in the Last Day so as to fear punishment. يُوادُّونَ is in the position of an accusative because it is the [second object, i.e.] khabar of تجد, or a naʿt (adjective) of قوم. وَلَوْ كانُوا آباءَهُمْ أَوْ أَبْناءَهُمْ أَوْ إِخْوانَهُمْ أَوْ عَشِيرَتَهُمْ i.e. even if those who opposed Allah and His Messenger were their fathers. [آباء is] the plural of أب according to the original [form]; its original is أبو, and the dual is also according to the original among the Basrans and nothing else, while the Kufans related: جاءني أبان. أَوْ أَبْناءَهُمْ is the plural of ابن according to the original; its original is بني, what has dropped from it being a yāʾ, while what has dropped from أب is a wāw. As for أب, the dual indicates it; as for ابن, the derivation indicates it.
Abū Isḥāq said: it is derived from "his father built him" (بناه أبوه), يبنيه [Translator's note: printed يبينه]. Abū Jaʿfar said: some of the grammarians erred and said: what dropped from it is a wāw, because البنوّة (sonship) has been heard. أَوْ إِخْوانَهُمْ is the plural of أخ according to the original, just as you say ورل and ورلان. أُولئِكَ كَتَبَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْإِيمانَ: it is said: it is figurative, and «في» has the meaning of the lām, i.e. He wrote faith for their hearts, it being known that the meaning is "He wrote for them"; and it is said: it is literal, i.e. He wrote in their hearts the mark of faith so that it is known that they are believers. وَأَيَّدَهُمْ بِرُوحٍ مِنْهُ: it is said: with light and guidance; and it is said: with Jibrāʾīl ﷺ, who helps them, supports them and grants them success. وَيُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها as a ḥāl (circumstantial). رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ i.e. for their obedience in this world. وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ for His admitting them into Paradise. أُولئِكَ حِزْبُ اللَّهِ i.e. His army and His company; and تحزّب القوم [means] the people gathered together. أَلا إِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ: it is said: i.e. those who attained what they wanted.
